chunks: 3. Al-Baqir (peace be upon him) said: My father Zayn al-Abidin (peace be upon him) narrated to me from his father al-Husayn ibn Ali (peace be upon them both) that he said:

The Samad (Needless) who has no cavity (hollow interior), the Samad whose tip has ended (is not hollow), the Samad who does not eat nor drink, the Samad who does not sleep, the Eternal Samad who has always been and will always be.

Al-Baqir (peace be upon him) said: Muhammad ibn al-Hanafiyyah (may Allah be pleased with him) used to say: The Samad is He who is self-sustaining, independent of others. And others said: The Samad is He who is exalted from creation and decay, and the Samad who is not described by change/diversity.
Al-Baqir (peace be upon him) said: The Samad is the Master who is obeyed, over whom there is no commander or forbider.
He (AS) said: Ali ibn al-Husayn Zayn al-Abidin (peace be upon them both) was asked about the Samad, so he said: The Samad is He who has no partner, whom nothing tires, and from whom nothing escapes.

key_terms.التَّغَايُر: Change or diversity, referring to alteration in attributes or state.
key_terms.الصَّمَدُ: The Samad (Needless/Perfect), a divine attribute meaning self-sufficient and having no internal void.
key_terms.الْغَنِيُّ: The Rich/Independent, needing nothing from others.
key_terms.الْفَسَاد: Decay or corruption, referring to the end of existence.
key_terms.الْقَائِمُ بِنَفْسِهِ: Self-sustaining, existing and maintaining oneself by one's own power.
key_terms.الْكَوْن: Creation/Existence, referring to coming into being.
key_terms.جَوْف: Cavity or hollow interior, used here to describe physical or metaphysical deficiency.
key_terms.سُؤْدَد: The tip or end of a thing, implying completeness or lack of a hollow end.

ai.seo_question: What does the term 'Al-Samad' mean in Shia theology according to Imam al-Baqir?
ai.summary: This hadith from Shaykh al-Saduq’s *al-Tawhid* offers a multi-layered exegesis of 'Al-Samad' by the Ahl al-Bayt, distinguishing between the physical metaphor of a solid, non-hollow entity and the metaphysical reality of absolute self-sufficiency (*al-Qa'im bi-nafsihi*). It synthesizes interpretations from Muhammad ibn al-Hanafiyyah and Ali ibn al-Husayn to emphasize God’s transcendence over creation (*al-Muta'ali 'an al-kawn*), eternal permanence, and unique authority, reinforcing the Shia understanding of divine unity as both ontological independence and supreme sovereignty.

en.sayed-ali-raza-rizvi: 3. Al-Baqir (AS) related: my father Zayn al-`Abidin (AS) said that His father, al-Husayn ibn `Ali (AS), said;

“The Needless [al-Samad] is He who has no deficiency [jawf]. He is the Possessor of Absolute Sovereignty. He does not eat or drink. He does not sleep. He is devoid of needs. He does not surrender and He does not have an end.”

Al-Baqir (AS) said: Muhammad ibn al-Hanafiyyah (RA) used to say: “The Needless [alSamad] is He who is Independent and Self-Sufficient {Ghani] from others. Someone other than him said: “The Needless is not subject to events and decline, and changes do not take place in Him.”
Al-Baqir (AS) Said: “The Needless [al-Samad] is the Obeyed Master who no one commander.”

He (AS) said: `Ali ibn al-Husayn Zayn al-`Abidin (AS) was asked about the Needless [alSamad], so he said: “The Needless is devoid of associates. Maintaining things does not tire Him, and nothing escapes Him.”
